message:
Structural Dynamicist and Serviceability and Crowd Loading Specialist, the device stays invisible from deck eye height with no change to walking feel.

The retrofit lives fully below the walking surface with no change to parapet, floor or sightlines. The Tuned Mass Damper (TMD), a sprung mass moving out of phase with the deck, uses moving mass 800 kg per the Den Hartog sizing (E11) and total hung load 9.81 kN per the hung load estimate (E29), about thirteen body weights and about a washing-machine cube, tucked between girders per the midspan layout sketch (E12).

Retrofit and Maintenance Engineer and the Manager, the device hides behind a girder-colour screen with fixed and moving parts separated and room to move.

Fixed parts are cross-beam, clamps and perforated screen, moving parts are springs plus damper plus mass free only vertically, with zero millimetres above the walking surface per the under-deck recessed cassette sketch (E30), and stroke 2.52 mm inside plus-minus 30 mm clearance per the damped response sweep (E32), a finger-nail travel that fits a shallow cassette, while damped peak 0.106 m/s2 is about 0.01 g like a still floor. Ready, because appearance, depth and below-deck install are frozen with buildable hardware.
